items.name: Margaï
items.desc: Margaï are the local spirits of the Hadjerai peoples of the Guéra and Salamat regions of Chad. They are present in family and village altars, often small pots called bourmas, and are served by ritual specialists known as the "masters of Margaï." The cult addresses health, marriage, birth, death, solemn oaths and the agricultural cycle, including the first storms and the harvest. Margaï are plural, can be benevolent or malevolent, and stand in relation to a supreme god; some are associated with panthers and lions.

items.name: The Universal Basilisk
items.desc: A legendary serpent or dragon, the Basilisk is known as the king of serpents, with a gaze and breath so venomous it can kill anything it encounters.

items.name: Nzame
items.desc: Nzame is the first person of the Fang trinity and the creator-father of Fang tradition. The Fang, who migrated from Cameroon toward Gabon, developed the trinity as a syncretic form drawing on their own mythology, Mitsogho and Mpongwe beliefs, and Christianity. Nzame Mebeghe holds the powers of the Father; Mebeghe is compared to Jesus Christ, and Gningone Mebeghe to Eve, the Virgin or the Holy Spirit. The trinity is the subject of theological speculation and of myths known to the fully initiated.
